USER GUIDE

01 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Start here

Bursara brings student fees, bills, receipts and unpaid balances into one workspace. This guide follows the application’s financial workflow.

How to use it

  1. Open https://app.bursara.com. Choose English or French in the language selector. Your choice is remembered across the website and application. Sign in with the account supplied by your institution.
  2. Create a course and its priced units, then enrol a student. A course is the full programme; a unit is a priced year, subject or module.
  3. Save an invoice draft and review it. An authorised user selects Post invoice. Record the money received as a payment draft, then select Post payment when authorised.
  4. Open the student account to review posted balances. Drafts do not affect the account totals. Use About this screen for a short explanation and a link to the relevant guide.

What to expect

BURARA CHILRENS ACADEMY is a protected shared demonstration. Use fictional learners, contacts and simulated payments. Other testers can see demonstration records.

This guide covers school financial administration. Attendance, check-in/check-out and timetables are not included.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd3 / 47
USER GUIDE

02 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Understand the money words

A few everyday terms make the rest of the screens easier to follow.

How to use it

  1. A bill or invoice says what a student or their responsible party owes. It can cover the whole year even when payment will come in smaller parts.
  2. A receipt acknowledges money already received. Recording a bill alone does not mean the school has received money.
  3. An allocation applies a received payment to a particular bill. The bill then shows a lower outstanding balance.
  4. An instalment is one scheduled amount and due date within a bill. Outstanding includes every unpaid amount; overdue includes only amounts whose due dates have passed.
  5. Unapplied credit is money received for a student that has not yet been used against a bill. A fee credit reduces a charge; a refund returns unused money.

What to expect

Example: a MUR 120,000 annual bill paid in twelve monthly instalments still starts as one MUR 120,000 bill. A MUR 25,000 allocated payment leaves MUR 95,000 outstanding. The overdue amount depends on the instalment dates and the selected balance date.

A bill, receipt and fee credit are different financial records even when an institution chooses a combined invoice/receipt workflow.

03 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Sign in and sign out

Sign in to reach the workspace your administrator has assigned to you.

How to use it

  1. If you have registered a passkey, select Sign in with passkey and follow your device’s verification prompt. Otherwise enter Email address and Password, then select Sign in.
  2. If the password method opens Verify your sign-in, enter the current code from your authenticator app or one unused recovery code. Select Verify and sign in.
  3. Institution users arrive at their own institution. Platform staff arrive at Client institutions. A verified passkey signs you in without a separate authenticator-code step.
  4. If the email or password is incorrect, check the spelling and try again. After five failed attempts for the same account and connection, wait the number of seconds shown.
  5. When finished, select Sign out at the bottom of the navigation menu. On a shared computer, close the browser after signing out.

What to expect

Your institution administrator creates ordinary user accounts and can set a new password through Users & permissions. A password reset does not remove an enabled authenticator. Bursara does not provide a self-service forgotten-password screen.

The shared demonstration login is protected. Its password cannot be changed and it cannot enrol passkeys or time-based one-time passwords. Private platform staff credentials are never included in this guide.

04 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Passkeys, verification and recovery

Sign-in security protects your own login. These options are available to institution users and platform staff; the shared demonstration login stays locked.

How to use it

  1. Open Sign-in security. Enter a Passkey name and select Add a passkey to register a device.
  2. Confirm it’s you asks for Current password and, if enabled, an Authenticator or recovery code. Select Continue and follow your device prompt.
  3. For app codes, select Set up authenticator app, confirm your identity, then privately scan the QR code or enter the setup key in your authenticator app.
  4. Enter Code from your authenticator app and select Enable authenticator. Password sign-in now needs a current app code or unused recovery code.
  5. Save the eight recovery codes privately using copy or download, then select I’ve saved these codes. Each works once. Replace recovery codes invalidates the old set.
  6. A verified passkey signs you in without a separate app code. Remove a retired key beside its name, or use Turn off authenticator to disable app codes, confirming your identity when asked.

What to expect

Keep setup keys and recovery codes private. If all sign-in methods are unavailable, contact your institution administrator or Bursara support.

The protected demonstration cannot enable these methods. An administrator changing your password does not remove existing passkeys or verification.

05 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Find your way around

The left menu groups the daily work. The floating help control explains the screen you are viewing.

How to use it

  1. Use Students for learners and their individual accounts. Use Courses & units for programmes and their fees.
  2. Use Billing for posted charges and Payments for received money and receipts.
  3. Use Debtors to follow unpaid fees. Reports contains currency summaries, the financial control journal and the balance export.
  4. Select About this screen at the lower right. Read the explanation, then select the same control again to close it.
  5. Open Sign-in security to protect your own login. If another menu item or action is missing, ask your administrator whether your user has the relevant permission.

What to expect

Saving or editing a draft does not affect financial totals. Posting an invoice or payment, allocating credit, issuing a fee credit or recording a refund does change the account.

Tables use a ledger layout and highlight rows on hover. Use the English/Français selector to change language; your choice is remembered.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd7 / 47
USER GUIDE

06 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Read the overview

The overview gives a quick account position for one currency and one date.

How to use it

  1. Choose Balance date. The figures use financial records up to that date, so changing it lets you review an earlier position.
  2. Choose Display currency. Each currency has its own figures; selecting USD does not convert every MUR transaction into dollars.
  3. Read the four totals: Fees billed, Payments received, Outstanding and Overdue. Fees billed also shows original net and VAT amounts.
  4. Look at unapplied student credit below the totals. This is received money still available to apply to a student's bills.
  5. Open a document in Recent bills or Recent collections, or use Create invoice draft and Create payment draft when your permissions allow them.

What to expect

Only posted financial records affect these figures. Saved drafts are excluded. Outstanding and overdue answer different questions. A future instalment is outstanding but is not overdue. An instalment due today becomes overdue only after that day has passed.

The overview is a starting point. Open the relevant bill, student account or report to understand a particular figure.

07 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Create a course

A course is the complete programme, such as High School or BSc Biomedical Sciences.

How to use it

  1. Open Courses & units and select New course.
  2. Enter Course name in language that school staff will recognise.
  3. Enter a short Code, such as HS. Codes must be unique within your institution.
  4. Optionally enter a Description, then select Create course.
  5. Add the priced units next. Creating the course by itself does not bill any student.

What to expect

For annual school billing, create one High School course and Year 1 to Year 4 units. For university billing, create the programme as the course and subjects as its units.

To correct an existing course, select Edit course, change its name, code or description and save. To change a unit, select Edit unit. Existing posted document lines keep their saved prices and descriptions.

08 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Set a fixed unit fee

Use a fixed fee when the price applies to the entire unit, such as one school year.

How to use it

  1. In Courses & units, select Add unit. Choose its Course.
  2. Enter Unit name and a unique Code. For example, use Year 1 and Y1.
  3. Enter Price and choose Currency. Enter amounts as numbers without currency symbols or thousands separators.
  4. Choose Fixed unit fee in Price basis. For a whole-year fee, leave Credits / weight as 1.
  5. Select Save unit. The unit will appear under its course and can be selected when enrolling a student.

What to expect

Example: Year 1 at a fixed MUR 120,000 price gives a MUR 120,000 fee for quantity 1, before discount or tax.

Use Edit unit to update the name, code, price, currency, price basis or credit weight. Changes apply to future selections. Review saved invoice drafts separately; posted lines keep their original amounts. Different unit currencies require separate invoices.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd10 / 47
USER GUIDE

09 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Set a fee per credit

Use a per-credit fee when the unit charge depends on its credit weight.

How to use it

  1. Select Add unit and choose the programme in Course.
  2. Enter the unit name and code, such as Cell Biology and BIO101.
  3. Enter the price for one credit in Price, then choose Currency.
  4. Choose Per credit in Price basis. Enter the number of credits in Credits / weight.
  5. Select Save unit. When this enrolled unit is selected on a bill, Bursara fills the quantity with its credit weight.

What to expect

Example: a unit with a USD 250 price per credit and a weight of 3 credits gives a USD 750 fee before discount or tax.

The posted bill uses the quantity and unit price shown on its fee line. Check them before posting. Unit prices support up to five decimal places and credit weights up to three; the final amount is rounded to the currency's normal precision.

10 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Enrol a student

Enrolment connects a learner, the party responsible for paying and the units that may be billed.

How to use it

  1. Open Students and select Enrol student. Enter Student name and a unique Student reference.
  2. Enter the Debtor / billing contact: the person or organisation responsible for the fees. Choose Parent / guardian, Student or Sponsor / employer under Responsible party.
  3. Optionally enter a student email, contact phone and billing address. Use fictional details while testing Bursara.
  4. Choose Course. Tick the Billable units in which the student is enrolled.
  5. Select Enrol student. Bursara opens the Student account. Check the learner, programme and billing contact.

What to expect

Units must belong to the chosen course. Enrol a learner in a priced unit before selecting it on their invoice; a custom fee can also be entered directly.

To update the learner, select Edit on the Students row or Edit student in the account. Review contacts, programme and selected units, then save. The student reference stays unique. Posted documents retain their original student details. Attendance and timetables are not included.

11 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Edit courses, units and students

Keep the catalogue and learner records current without rewriting posted documents.

How to use it

  1. In Courses & units, choose Edit course to change the name, unique code or description. Save the course.
  2. Choose Edit unit to change its name, code, price, currency, price basis or credits. An enrolled unit cannot be moved to another course; create a new unit instead.
  3. In Students choose Edit, or open an account and choose Edit student. Review the reference, contact details, responsible party, course and selected units, then save.
  4. When changing the course, select only units belonging to the new course. Review the selected units before saving.
  5. Existing drafts do not silently take new unit prices. Open Edit draft and review its lines. Posted invoices and receipts retain their saved amounts and student details.

What to expect

Manage courses and fees controls catalogue changes. Manage students controls learner changes. An edit never grants access to another institution.

There is no deletion or student promotion workflow here. Verify references and contacts before saving.

12 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Reuse products and fee templates

Save reusable tuition, university, transport and other charges, then select them on one-off or recurring invoices.

How to use it

  1. Open Products & prices and select Create product. Enter Product name, a unique Product code, Description, Default quantity, Price and Currency.
  2. Choose Availability scope: Institution-wide, One learner, One enrolled unit or One programme. A unit-linked product requires enrolment in that unit; a programme-linked product requires the learner’s current programme.
  3. Keep inherited tax settings, or configure a product tax override where appropriate. Review whether the entered price includes or excludes tax.
  4. Select Save product. In an invoice draft or recurring template, choose the learner and select an available product on the fee line. Check its copied description, quantity, price and preview.
  5. Review quantity, discounts, dates and totals, then save the draft or schedule. Posting remains a separate authorised action.

What to expect

Products stay within your institution. Manage products controls catalogue changes; billing users can select eligible products. Their currency must match the invoice. Selecting a product copies its price, quantity and description; catalogue edits do not rewrite existing lines.

Deactivate a product to stop future selections, or reactivate it when needed. There is no delete action. Existing drafts and posted documents keep their snapshots. Freeform fees remain available without a product. Review recurring templates when a linked product becomes unavailable.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd14 / 47
USER GUIDE

13 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Set VAT defaults and line overrides

Choose tax treatment and price mode, then understand which setting applies to a fee line.

How to use it

  1. In Settings, find Institution VAT defaults. Review VAT-registered institution and the optional registration number.
  2. Choose VAT treatment and VAT rate (%). Taxable requires registration and a positive rate. Zero-rated, Exempt and Outside the scope of VAT remain separate classifications. New institutions start unregistered, outside scope, at a zero rate.
  3. Choose Price mode, then Save VAT defaults. Inclusive prices contain tax; exclusive prices have tax added. Discounts reduce the line amount before VAT is calculated.
  4. Override defaults in a course, unit, product or invoice line as needed. To inherit again, select Inherit tax treatment and Inherit price mode and leave the rate blank.
  5. Check the price preview’s Net amount, VAT amount and Gross amount before saving a draft. Posting remains a separate authorised action.

What to expect

Priority is line override, product, unit, course, then institution. A freeform line uses institution defaults; choosing a learner alone does not apply course tax settings. The institution’s stored rate may still supply fees configured as Taxable even when its own default treatment has no VAT charge.

Changing defaults alone does not alter a saved draft. Explicitly editing and saving it resolves inherited tax again; manual line overrides stay fixed. Posting preserves the reviewed snapshot. Future recurring drafts resolve current inherited tax, while their template prices stay saved until the schedule is edited.

14 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Use a student account

The student account brings one learner's bills and receipts together.

How to use it

  1. Open Students, search by name, reference or debtor, and select the student name or open arrow.
  2. Check the learner and billing-contact details. These identify the account being reviewed.
  3. Read the outstanding amount and unapplied credit for each currency. Different currencies stay separate.
  4. Use the Fee register to open a bill. Use the Receipt register to open a receipt.
  5. Select Create invoice draft, Create payment draft or Print statement as needed. Your permissions determine which actions are available.

What to expect

The student account is useful when a parent or sponsor asks what remains to be paid. Open the individual bill to see its monthly due dates and exactly how payments have been applied.

Unapplied credit is shown separately from outstanding fees. It does not settle a bill until you explicitly apply it.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd16 / 47
USER GUIDE

15 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Choose the billing workflow

Choose how the charge and the collection should be recorded before posting.

How to use it

  1. Open Billing and select Create invoice draft. Choose the Student and Billing workflow.
  2. Choose Bill first, collect later for a charge that will be collected separately. Choose Assessed fees with instalments for an assessment with scheduled due amounts.
  3. Choose Receive full payment and issue only when the entire charge has already been received. Its payment method and reference are saved with the draft.
  4. Select Save draft, then review the draft document. Select Edit draft to correct it before posting.
  5. An authorised user selects Post invoice. For the combined workflow, this posts the invoice and its full payment together; otherwise record payments separately.

What to expect

Saving a draft requires Create and edit invoice drafts. Posting requires Post invoices; the combined workflow also requires Post payments. Saving a draft does not bill a student or acknowledge received money.

A draft receives a permanent SO-00001 creation reference. Its final INV000001 number is assigned only when posted. Draft edits consume no final invoice numbers. SO and PO are creation references, not sales or purchase orders.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd17 / 47

16 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Review, edit and post a draft

A saved draft is a preparation step. Posting makes the financial document effective.

How to use it

  1. Open Billing or Payments and find the SO or PO creation reference. Use the Draft status filter if needed.
  2. Open the draft and review learner, dates, currency, amounts and fee lines or proposed allocations. No account balance has changed yet.
  3. With Create and edit invoice drafts or Create and edit payment drafts, choose Edit draft. Make the correction and save. The permanent creation reference stays the same.
  4. An authorised user selects Post invoice or Post payment. The final INV or REC number is assigned only now, and balances and the journal are updated.
  5. If a payment allocation is refused because another operation settled the bill, edit the draft to match the current balance. Search the register before creating a replacement.

What to expect

Posted documents cannot be edited. Use a separate approved credit or refund where supported. Repeating a post request does not create another financial document.

A submitted fiscal draft cannot be edited, even when its provider result is rejected or uncertain. An unsubmitted prepared snapshot is invalidated when its draft changes.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd18 / 47
USER GUIDE

17 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Schedule recurring fee drafts

Prepare repeating school, university or bus fees automatically, then review and post each invoice separately.

How to use it

  1. Open Recurring billing and select Create schedule. Enter Schedule name and choose the Student.
  2. Choose Frequency: Weekly, Monthly, Every three months, Every four months, Every six months or Yearly. Set Start date and optional End date.
  3. Choose currency and fee lines, using enrolled units or custom school, university or bus charges. Set Days until first payment is due and Monthly instalments.
  4. Select Save schedule. The next occurrence appears in Billing schedules. A future schedule waits until its date; the end date limits future occurrences.

What to expect

Each occurrence prepares a separate draft using the saved fee template. It does not post an invoice, collect money or submit a fiscal document.

For a one-off charge, use Create invoice draft in Billing. Monthly instalments divide a single invoice; recurrence prepares separate invoices.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd19 / 47
USER GUIDE

18 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Manage recurring drafts and schedules

Review generated drafts, pause future generation and keep posting under separate control.

How to use it

  1. Active schedules automatically prepare due drafts. Generate due drafts runs due occurrences now. Future dates wait until they arrive.
  2. View generated drafts opens the history and SO references. Open each draft, review it and use Edit draft if needed. An authorised user selects Post invoice; no payment is recorded by the schedule.
  3. Edit schedule changes the future template. Pause stops generation; Resume restarts it. Existing drafts and posted documents stay unchanged.
  4. If generation reports a problem, check the visible message, learner enrolment and template. Correct the cause before generating again; do not create another schedule just to retry.

What to expect

Schedule changes require Create and edit invoice drafts; posting needs Post invoices. After the first draft, start date and frequency are fixed. Create a new schedule to change them.

Monthly dates retain the original day where possible. Pausing preserves the next occurrence, so resuming can catch up missed dates. Template edits affect future drafts only; existing drafts and posted documents stay unchanged.

19 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Create an annual school bill

Bill the whole school year once and then collect the money over time.

How to use it

  1. Create the bill, select the student and choose Bill first, collect later. Enter Issue date and Service period, such as Academic year 2027.
  2. Choose the school year in Enrolled unit. Check Description, Quantity / credits and Unit price. Use Add line for another charge.
  3. Confirm Currency. When it differs from the functional currency, enter the rate requested by the form. Review discounts and tax.
  4. Enter First due date and Monthly instalments, then select Save draft. The draft has an SO creation reference and does not affect outstanding fees.
  5. Review the saved document. Use Edit draft to correct it. An authorised user selects Post invoice to assign its final invoice number and create the charge.

What to expect

A unit price of MUR 120,000 with quantity 1 is one annual fee before any VAT. Twelve instalments change when the bill is due, not its total. Check the VAT treatment and price mode in the preview.

Posted records are immutable. Correct an unpaid charge using an authorised separate fee credit rather than changing the original invoice.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd21 / 47
USER GUIDE

20 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Set monthly instalments

The schedule says when parts of a bill fall due. It does not create extra invoices or extra fees.

How to use it

  1. In the invoice draft form, enter First due date on or after Issue date.
  2. Choose Monthly instalments. Use One payment due when the full charge is due on one date.
  3. Add Notes, select Save draft and inspect the proposed schedule. Use Edit draft if the dates or amounts need correction.
  4. Select Post invoice when authorised. Check Payment schedule on the posted document. The final invoice number is assigned at this point.
  5. Save and post payment drafts as money arrives. Confirmed allocations pay the earliest unpaid instalments first.

What to expect

MUR 120,000 over twelve instalments gives MUR 10,000 each. Bursara distributes rounding remainders so the schedule always equals the exact invoice total.

Monthly dates retain the chosen day where possible: 31 January is followed by 28 or 29 February, then 31 March. Recurring billing prepares separate invoice drafts; each is reviewed and posted separately.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd22 / 47

21 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Bill university units

Use one or more enrolled units instead of a whole-year school fee.

How to use it

  1. Create an invoice draft for the learner. Enter Service period, such as Semester 1 / 2027.
  2. Choose an Enrolled unit. For a per-credit fee, check the filled Quantity / credits and price for one credit.
  3. Check Currency and the requested Rate. Add further units in the same currency with Add line.
  4. Enter the due schedule and select Save draft. Open Edit draft to correct the subjects, quantity or prices before posting.
  5. Select Post invoice when authorised. Confirm its final number and posted schedule. Create another invoice for units in a different currency.

What to expect

Three credits at USD 250 give a USD 750 line. A fixed USD 400 laboratory fee can be added as a second line with quantity 1.

The invoice saves its own descriptions, prices, student details and rate. Later catalogue or student edits do not rewrite posted documents.

22 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Receive full payment and issue together

Use this workflow when the entire fee is paid at the time you issue the document.

How to use it

  1. Create an invoice draft and choose Receive full payment and issue in Billing workflow.
  2. Complete the student, dates, currency and fee lines. Select Payment method and enter Payment reference where available.
  3. Select Save draft. Review its SO creation reference, fee total and proposed payment details. No charge or receipt is posted yet.
  4. Only when the full amount has really arrived, an authorised user selects Post invoice. This requires both Post invoices and Post payments.
  5. Open the resulting invoice and receipt. Check the final INV and REC numbers and zero Outstanding balance.

What to expect

Posting completes the full invoice and payment together. Repeating the post action does not create another charge or receipt.

For a partial collection, post an ordinary invoice and prepare a separate payment draft. Bursara records a payment method but does not initiate bank transfers or charge cards.

23 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Read a posted invoice

The posted invoice is the record of the charge, its payments and its unpaid balance.

How to use it

  1. In Billing, open the invoice number. Check the institution, student, billing contact, date and service period.
  2. Review each line: description, quantity, unit price, discount, tax and amount.
  3. Read Net amount, VAT amount, Total fees, Payments applied, Credits and Outstanding. Check the Payment schedule below.
  4. Use Receive payment to prepare a collection, or Credit outstanding fees for an approved reduction of unpaid charges.

What to expect

The permanent SO reference stays alongside the INV number assigned at posting. Outstanding includes future unpaid instalments. Posted invoices cannot be edited: use a separate credit where supported. Fiscal documents require their local correction process.

Older documents may show a VAT rate with treatment not recorded. Their saved amounts remain intact; do not infer an exemption from a zero rate.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd25 / 47
USER GUIDE

24 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Record a partial payment

Record only the money actually received, then apply it to the student's bill.

How to use it

  1. Open an unpaid invoice and select Receive payment. The student and bill are preselected.
  2. Enter the Amount received. If MUR 25,000 arrived, enter 25000 even when the full bill is MUR 120,000.
  3. Check Received date, Method, Payer and Reference. Use a bank transfer only after it is confirmed, or Cleared cheque only after it has cleared.
  4. In Allocate to bills, leave the correct bill selected and enter the portion to apply in Apply (MUR).
  5. Select Save draft. Review the saved payment, use Edit draft if needed, then select Post payment when authorised. Open the bill again and check its new Outstanding amount.

What to expect

A payment draft receives a permanent PO-00001 creation reference but changes no balance. Post payment assigns REC000001 and records the money and allocations. Create and edit payment drafts and Post payments are separate rights.

MUR 25,000 applied to a posted MUR 120,000 bill leaves MUR 95,000 outstanding. Posting rechecks the latest invoice balance; if another receipt has settled it, edit the draft allocations before trying again.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd26 / 47
USER GUIDE

25 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Allocate one payment to bills

An allocation tells Bursara which unpaid charge the received money should settle.

How to use it

  1. Open Payments and select Create payment draft. Choose the student and fill in the received amount, date, currency and method.
  2. Under Allocate to bills, tick each bill that this payment should help settle.
  3. Enter the amount to apply for each selected bill. The total used from the payment must not exceed Amount received.
  4. Leave a bill unticked when this payment is not intended for it. Any unused received money remains unapplied student credit.
  5. Select Save draft. Review the saved payment, use Edit draft if needed, then select Post payment when authorised. Review Applied to fees on the receipt and follow an invoice link to check its balance.

What to expect

A payment can be applied to several bills for the same student. It cannot be applied to another student's bill or to another institution.

For one currency, the applied bill amount and the amount used from the payment are the same. For different currencies, you must enter both sides, as explained in the next procedure.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd27 / 47
USER GUIDE

26 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Receive a payment in another currency

Record the currency received and the amount of the bill that it settles as two separate amounts.

How to use it

  1. Open Receive a payment and choose the payment Currency. Enter Amount received in that currency.
  2. Enter the Rate requested by the form. Read the label carefully: Rate: 1 USD in MUR means how many MUR equal one USD.
  3. Tick the bill being paid. Enter Apply (MUR) as the amount to remove from the MUR bill.
  4. Enter Uses (USD) as the part of the USD payment used for that allocation.
  5. Check both amounts and the rate, then select Save draft, review it and select Post payment when authorised. Review the currencies shown in Applied to fees.

What to expect

Example: the school receives USD 100 and agrees that this settles MUR 4,600 of a bill. Enter 100 received, 4600 in Apply (MUR), 100 in Uses (USD), and the appropriate rate of 46.

Bursara does not fetch exchange rates automatically. Your institution must supply the correct rate and agreed settlement amounts. MUR, USD and most supported currencies use two decimal places; JPY uses none and KWD uses three.

Bursara | Streak Technologies Ltd28 / 47
USER GUIDE

27 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Record an advance payment

Keep money received before it is assigned to a bill as unapplied student credit.

How to use it

  1. Open Payments and select Create payment draft. Select the correct Student and Payer.
  2. Enter Amount received, Currency, Received date, Method and any Reference.
  3. Under Allocate to bills, leave every bill unticked. If the student has no unpaid bills, the form explains that the money will be held as credit.
  4. Select Save draft. Review it, then select Post payment when authorised. Review Unapplied credit on the receipt.
  5. Keep the receipt reference. Later, open it to apply available credit to a bill or refund unused money.

What to expect

Save and post an advance even when there is no invoice. Posting records received money as unapplied credit; it settles no invoice until explicitly allocated.

The PO creation reference stays with the payment after its REC receipt number is assigned. For a payment received before an invoice date, leave it unapplied first, then apply credit with a valid later date.

Apply existing student credit

Use an earlier unapplied payment against an outstanding bill without recording the money twice.

How to use it

  2. If credit remains and a same-currency bill is unpaid, select Apply student credit.
  3. Choose the Outstanding invoice. Enter Apply amount (MUR), or the currency shown.
  4. Enter Allocation date. It cannot be earlier than the original payment, the bill or a refund already recorded against that payment.
  5. Select Apply credit to bill. Check that the receipt's unapplied credit and the bill's outstanding amount both decrease.

What to expect

This is an application of money already received. Do not use Receive payment again for the same money.

Refund unused credit

Record money returned from the part of a payment that has not been applied to bills.

How to use it

  3. Enter Date. The refund cannot predate the original payment.

Reduce an outstanding fee

A fee credit reduces a charge that remains unpaid, for example an approved scholarship adjustment.

How to use it

  2. Enter Amount in the invoice currency. It cannot exceed the current outstanding balance.

Set the right permissions

Bursara checks these permissions whenever someone tries an action.

How to use it

  1. Open Users & permissions and select Edit permissions for an ordinary user.
  2. Manage students allows creating and editing learners. Manage courses and fees allows creating and editing programmes and units. Manage products separately authorises reusable fee templates.
  3. Create and edit invoice drafts allows saving and correcting drafts. Post invoices separately authorises posting. Create and edit payment drafts and Post payments follow the same separation.

Permissions do not change which institution the person belongs to. An empty checkbox selection grants none of the listed action rights. Your account cannot remove its own user-management access here.

42 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Prepare and review a sandbox fiscal document

Preparing a fiscal document and submitting it are separate actions in Bursara.

How to use it

  1. In Modules, select the eligible Invoice and, in payment mode, its allocated Payment. Eligibility follows the saved event and Draft or Posted stage.
  2. Select Prepare sandbox document. This saves a snapshot in Fiscal register; it does not send it to EBS.
  3. Select Review. Check the institution, amounts, currency, event and the separate fiscal reference. EBS uses its own continuous fiscal numbering; SO and PO remain creation references.
  4. An authorised tester with test credentials may select Submit to sandbox. Ordinary billing exercises need no submission.
  5. For a queued reference, use Refresh status. Reconcile an Unknown result with EBS before retrying or preparing another reference.

What to expect

An unsubmitted prepared snapshot is invalidated if its financial draft changes, so prepare it again after review. A submitted fiscal draft is locked against financial editing, including rejected or uncertain submissions.

EBS preparation supports 15% taxable, zero-rated, exempt or outside-scope service lines only when their saved totals can be represented exactly. Payment reporting requires allocated zero-tax tuition with one consistent treatment. Prepared is not accepted; Unknown needs reconciliation. Live submissions and fiscal credit notes are not included.

44 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Solve common problems

Use the message on the screen to decide the next step. Avoid creating a second transaction to solve an uncertain first attempt.

How to use it

  1. Cannot sign in: check email and password, or use a registered passkey. If Verify your sign-in appears, use your authenticator app or an unused recovery code. After repeated failures, wait for the displayed delay. Ask the institution administrator for account help. If a verification code was just used, wait for the next code in your app.
  2. Missing button or access denied: ask an administrator to review your permission checkboxes. Client users cannot enter another institution.
  3. Unit missing from a bill: check the student's chosen course and enrolled units. Units from another course or another currency cannot be silently combined.
  4. Payment will not post: check decimal precision, positive amounts, dates and allocations. Applied amounts cannot exceed the bill or available payment.
  5. Credit or refund blocked: a fee credit cannot exceed unpaid fees; a refund cannot exceed unused student credit. Fiscal documents need their country-specific e-invoicing correction process.
  6. Unknown fiscal result: stop and reconcile the original reference. Do not submit it again just because a response was slow.

What to expect

If you are unsure whether a bill or payment was posted, first search Billing or Payments and open the student account. Check for the existing document before trying another transaction.

When reporting a problem, give the screen name, document number, steps taken, expected outcome and exact visible message. Use fictional records and remove confidential information from screenshots.

45 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Help, boundaries and quick reference

Use this final page as a short reminder and a route to support.

How to use it

  1. Institution: one school, college or learning organisation with its own isolated records.
  2. Course: the whole programme. Unit: a priced year, subject, module or other part of that programme.
  3. Debtor: the student, parent, guardian, employer or sponsor responsible for paying.
  4. Functional currency: the institution's main reporting currency. Document currency: the currency on a particular bill or receipt.
  5. Fee credit: a separate reduction of an unpaid charge. Student credit: money received but not yet applied. Refund: money returned from unused credit.
  6. For product help, contact support@streaktechnologies.com, +230 215 2998, or visit streaktechnologies.com.

What to expect

Bursara is a product of Streak Technologies Ltd, Royal Road, Pointe aux Cannoniers, Grand Bay, Mauritius. USA contact: +1 307 500 3256.

This guide covers courses, reusable products, VAT defaults, learner records, editable drafts, authorised posting, receipts, instalments, recurring draft schedules, debtor balances, access rights, personal sign-in protection and optional Mauritius test reporting. Attendance, timetables, online collections, accounting integration are not included.
